title: Regional and social differences concerning overweight, participation in health check-ups and vaccination. Analysis of data from a whole birth cohort of 6-year old children in a prosperous German city.
ehr_evidence: The main basis for the analyses are the data from the medical check-up of the cohort starting school in 2004, provided by the Department for Health and Environment of the City of Munich, Germany.
summary: A cross-sectional multilevel analysis of 9,353 six-year-old children in a whole 2004 Munich school cohort examining individual and regional social differences in overweight, preventive health check-up participation, and vaccination.
key_findings: Prevalence of overweight (BMI ≥90th percentile) was 10.29%, incomplete U1-U9 check-ups 23.15%, and incomplete immunizations 55.14%.

Non-German mother tongue was associated with about three times higher overweight risk (OR 2.96, 95% CI 2.56-3.42) and higher incomplete check-ups (OR 2.94, 95% CI 2.63-3.28) versus German mother tongue.
Non-German mother tongue was associated with lower incomplete immunizations (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.55-0.66), an opposite association.
Kindergarten visit 'no' was associated with higher incomplete check-ups (OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.67-2.56) and incomplete immunizations (OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.07-1.59).

High percentage of low-education households was associated with higher overweight (OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.47-2.24) and incomplete check-ups (OR 1.63, 95% CI 1.40-1.90) and lower immunizations (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.68-0.88) with a dose-response pattern.
In multilevel analysis, high percentage of single-parent households was associated with lower incomplete immunizations (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.73-0.94) only.
No school district showed problematic values (high overweight, low check-ups, low immunizations) for all three variables simultaneously.
captured_features: Participation in preventive health check-ups U1-U9
Percentage of households with lowest educational level (school district)
study_design: Cross-sectional multilevel analysis of a whole birth/school cohort
population: 9,353 six-year-old children (2004 Munich school cohort) in Munich, Germany
exposure_domain: Individual and regional social/socioeconomic factors (migration background, single-parent households, low educational level)
limitations: Dataset includes only a few variables on health and health-related risks for each child.
No environmental factors (traffic noise, air pollution, availability of parks/playgrounds) could be included at the regional level.
Limited social indicators per child/family; no detailed social status information.
Some health variables (e.g., vision/hearing) were assessed imprecisely and disregarded.
Overweight classification based on the 90th percentile German definition.
